charges: Arson
sentence: Charged with arson after a May 30-31, 2020 protest near a shopping plaza on East Fowler Avenue devolved into unrest and looting. Video showed him tossing a flaming cloth through a broken window of the Champs Sports store; the building was fully engulfed and the plaza suffered about $1.25 million in damage. Sentenced to 60 months in federal prison plus 36 months supervised release.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida

charges: Arson (conspiracy)
sentence: Charged with co-defendants Kenyatta Huggins and Shamyrin Johnson for the May 31 - June 1, 2020 arsons at four Baton Rouge-area businesses. Admitted starting the fires, saying he was angry about anti-police tensions. Sentenced to 18 months in federal prison.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, Middle District of Louisiana

charges: Assaulting a federal officer
sentence: Charged with assaulting a federal officer on July 5, 2020 during Portland protests following the murder of George Floyd; a Reed College student, he was arrested at a violent protest on July 6, 2020. Found not guilty at trial.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, District of Oregon

charges: Possession of firearms and ammunition by an unlawful user of controlled substances
sentence: Charged in Minneapolis after resisting arrest at a protest outside the Government Center during the summer 2020 wave following the murder of George Floyd; seen reaching for his waistband, which held a loaded handgun. Sentenced to time served plus 2 years supervised release.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, District of Minnesota

charges: Arson
sentence: Involved in an arson of the Shaia's parking-lot attendant booth on May 30, 2020 during the George Floyd protests. The government dismissed the indictment and supplemental information without prejudice.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, Northern District of Ohio

charges: Aggravated rioting, vandalism
sentence: Arrested June 1, 2020 for helping pull a granite civil-rights plaque off the Historic Metro Courthouse (Nashville City Hall) wall; the smashed pieces were used to break courthouse windows. Filmed on Facebook Live ripping off the memorial while encouraging others. Sentenced to 48 months in Tennessee state prison.
institution_name: Tennessee state prison (Davidson County)

charges: Civil disorder, assault on a police officer, criminal mischief
sentence: Arrested June 12, 2020 for civil disorder and assaulting a police officer at a Black Lives Matter protest in Houston, and charged with shattering windows on police department vehicles during the George Floyd uprising. In February 2022 the charges were dismissed by the judge.
institution_name: Harris County District Court

charges: Attempted arson, possession of a destructive device
sentence: Charged in Milwaukee in June 2020 after throwing a Molotov cocktail through the window of a Boost Mobile store. Granted conditions of release; a violation would expose him to up to 10 years in federal prison or a $250,000 fine.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Wisconsin

charges: Arson
sentence: Charged with one count of arson in Manhattan for attempting to set a police car on fire by lighting a cloth glove and placing it under the vehicle. Prosecutors said it could be charged federally because the NYPD receives federal funds. Charged but not tried.
institution_name: New York County Supreme Court

charges: Arson (conspiracy)
sentence: Charged in a conspiracy with Shador T.C. Jackson and Leroy L.P. Williams for fires set inside Target's world headquarters in Minneapolis on August 26, 2020; in the mailroom Edwards added liquid accelerant to a fire Jackson had started. Sentenced to 60 months on count 1 and 100 months on count 2, served concurrently.
institution_name: U.S. District Court, District of Minnesota

charges: Vandalism
sentence: Arrested June 3, 2020 for vandalism at the Nashville Historic Courthouse; police say video and photos show him using objects to break at least two courthouse windows on May 30, 2020 after a peaceful protest over the death of George Floyd. Sentenced to 1.6 months in Tennessee state prison plus supervised probation.
institution_name: Tennessee state prison (Davidson County)
